Adshaw (Z26)

Verification: 13 October 2026 | Local Mod v1.37.5.0 | Survey-table region: Wescann / Gerudia.

Story quality: High; based primarily on local narrative | Mission-tree length: 72 direct missions | Mission-tree update context: current installation v1.37.5.0; the author's actual last update is unverified | Distinctiveness: High; build spy networks, assassinate target rulers, install your dynasty and subject neighbouring Reach states | Downtime (lower means smoother): Medium; diplomatic, research or event-state prerequisites apply | Opening pressure: 77/100, not an in-game difficulty test | Expansion demand: 84/100, driven by both warfare and statecraft.

v2.1: E82 · A78 · M/T50 · I12 · P42; values: Neutral (47), trajectory stable. The five axes are not a four-letter type; see the separate v2.2 conditional route profiles.

Overview for players

Adshaw's great appeal is that it turns the spy network, usually used to fabricate claims, into a genuine political weapon. You do not overwhelm the world with a spectacular mage or a unique piece of artificery. Instead, you cultivate relationships among the Reach states and create fractures, making other people's thrones, nobles and protection agreements serve your interests. In time, the small state's intrigues can reshape the northern order. Players who enjoy setting the pieces before closing the net are more likely to enjoy it than those who only want to fight one major war after another.

Historical background and the 1444 situation

Established history. Adshaw is a feudal lordship in the Alenic Reach. The English offline Wiki describes it as a lordship centred on Rycastle; current local history explicitly records Old Alenic culture, Regent Court religion and Rycan IV's accession in 1432. Queen Myra is from Z45, and Bayvic and Celmaldor are listed as historical rivals. The king's Charismatic Negotiator personality and relationship-network traits also echo the court manoeuvring that follows.

The Reach is prosperous but divided, and the tension between old rule and urban independence provides important context for the mission narrative. However, the opening scripts do not give a complete history of every neighbouring revolt; summaries from other countries' DOCX files cannot be transplanted into an authoritative Adshaw chronology. What can be established is that you face a region already shaped by its own rulers, nobles and diplomatic interests, not an ungoverned blank space waiting to be conquered.

Signature mechanics and campaign rhythm

The opening builds military strength and access to leaders, then quickly reaches Adshaw's signature, “The Serpent in the Bay.” Depending on conditions, the mission requires 30 or 50 spy-network points. If target Z32 still exists and is not already controlled by another country in the relevant way, the reward is not an ordinary diplomatic bonus: it kills the ruler, installs a new monarch from Adshaw's dynasty and makes the target a subject. Alternative conditions account for prior control or a target that no longer exists, so one outcome should not be described as an animation guaranteed in every save.

The Border Cove line is similarly concrete: build a spy network, use agents, bribes and promises of titles to incite the nobility against the merchants, then use protection and follow-up events to change the city's allegiance. Diplomacy becomes part of expansion rather than a pause between wars. You must track whether the target exists, who controls it and which conditional branch applies; annexing every neighbour too early can change the story you encounter.

The middle and late campaign still involve warfare, port and fleet construction, and the management of a wider northern realm. This is not a pure espionage minigame: indirect rule, military integration and economic development form a long campaign. Seventy-two direct missions provide substantial content, but the count does not mean 72 equally long, independent stories.

The future in the mission tree

Mission-tree future. Neighbouring crises, integration of the Reach, expansion into the uplands and northern political reorganisation gradually broaden Adshaw's objectives. Clovibian missions also branch into different event text according to campaign victory or defeat, or the 1475 date, and swap in non-generic mission trees. The success narrative emphasises a shared future with the Frozenmaw frontier; failure preserves the reality of eastern orc control. These differences are conditional outcomes of the campaign.

Do not package the cooperation narrative as “the player's peaceful route,” or describe defeat as another freely selected evil ending. The acceptance or refusal in the Border Cove event is first of all the target country's choice, not two identities available to Adshaw's player. This representative review did not confirm a fixed Tag-changing successor or a major permanent mutually exclusive route, so the article retains one baseline personality and describes the outcome-dependent phase separately.

National personality and values

Adshaw is a politically enterprising state with high expansion and authority, and low dependence on magic or artificery. It builds and reorganises the region, but does so through substantial manipulation; pluralist integration therefore receives only limited credit, and having subjects is not assumed to mean respecting their autonomy. Compared with Khozrugan, Adshaw relies more on political networks; compared with Corvuria, equally severe supernatural violations of personhood have not been established.

The value judgment concerns assassination, agent-provoked revolt and replacement of rulers, not “monarchy is bad.” Public works and a conditional future of cooperation mean that Adshaw should not be reduced to a state with no purpose beyond destruction. Its classification is Neutral: the darkness lies mainly in political manoeuvring. A single line about protecting people does not erase the concrete methods described above.

Community experience, recommendations and cautions

Community opinion. Two player discussions whose substantive posts were retrieved emphasise that espionage, revolt and Reach diplomacy give the older mission tree a distinctive identity, while also warning about powerful northern neighbours and the constrained opening space. They date from 2023 and 2026; their versions and opening conditions should not be conflated with a current strength test. This review did not find an independent official development diary substantively about Adshaw; passing mentions in diaries about other countries do not count as an Adshaw diary.

Recommended for players who enjoy subjects, court intrigue and long-term planning. Not for those who want to clear the mission tree using the simplest possible sequence of war declarations. The difficulty assessment comes from the conditional structure and player context; no campaign was played through in this review, so no particular alliance combination is guaranteed to work.

See the evidence page for sources, retrieval scope and unresolved points.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Adshaw (Z26) — Adshawman Ideas

Set ID: Z26_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z26
    }

Adshawman Traditions

  • global_regiment_cost: -10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Domestic trade power: +10% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

1. Men of Oak

The average Adshawman grows up hunting wild beasts, felling the titanic trees that loom over our realm, and lugging great trunks to sawmills. Our people possess a great strength and sturdiness because of this bucolic upbringing, rumoured to rival that of even an orc.

  • Infantry combat ability: +15% (infantry_power; raw value 0.15).

2. Sovereigns of the Reach

Before the knife-eared bastards of Celmaldor incited our subjects to rebel, and before those pesky Blue Reachmen had a notion of independence, the Kingdom of Adshaw ruled over much of the western Alenic Reach, reining in the notoriously rebellious Reachmen and their cities, and establishing a realm powerful enough to withstand the Kingdom of Gawed itself. Even if we may have fallen far from such glory, all remember when the banner of Rygan flew across the Serpentshead.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

3. Greatwood Fortresses

Our lands have a great lack of good stone to build forts out of, therefore the majority of our bastions are primarily constructed out of Greatwood Oak, of which we have plenty of to repair any damages.

  • Fort defense: +10% (defensiveness; raw value 0.1).

  • Fort maintenance: -10% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.1).

4. House of Rygan

Adshaw was founded by the great chieftain of the Adderic tribe, Rygan of Adderwood. The Adshaw dynasty has always and will always rule this realm, through all her glory and tribulations, forging a sense of unity and brotherhood amongst the once rivalled tribes of the northern Greatwoods.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

5. Lessons of Coldmarket

The Ambush at Coldmarket in 1024 marked the end of the Kingdom of Adshaw. While marching to finally quell the last remnants of the Blue Reachmen Wars of Independence in Coldmarket, King Rylen of Adshaw's forces were ambushed by a secret coalition of rotten elves from Celmaldor and Blue Reachmen separatists. We were used to the tactics of the Blue Reachmen, yes, but the elven-eyed archers overwhelmed our forces and led to their shattering when an arrow met with our king. Since then, we've developed several tactics and formations to avoid such a disaster from happening again.

  • fire_damage_received: -10% (fire_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

6. Every Man A Warrior

Since the days of Rygan and the dozen tribes of the Greatwoods, every able man has been required to keep themselves and their weapons in good shape, and be fully prepared to take up arms in the name of his lord and sovereign.

  • Land force limit modifier: +10% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Reinforce speed: +10% (reinforce_speed; raw value 0.1).

7. Adshaw Fur

We have plenty of creatures to gather furs from, bears, wolves, werewolves, beavers, and other such mammals stalk our woods, and are harvested by our woodsmen.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

Adshawman Ambition

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).
